entities.name: Pelicar
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pelicar, also known as Pellicar or Belicar, was a Guanche *mencey* (king) who ruled the Menceyato of Icode on the island of Tenerife during the critical period of its Castilian conquest in the late 15th century (circa 1494–1496). As one of the nine indigenous monarchs of Tenerife, his leadership embodied the final vestiges of pre-colonial Guanche sovereignty in the face of burgeoning European expansion. His significance lies in his role as a direct participant in the ultimate, tragic defense of his people and land against the technologically superior forces of the Crown of Castile, a pivotal moment in the integration of the Canary Islands into what would become the Spanish Empire.

Pelicar’s *menceyato*, Icode, was situated in the northwestern part of Tenerife, one of the so-called "rebel" kingdoms that initially resisted Castilian incursions. Alongside other Guanche leaders such as Bencomo of Taoro, Pelicar was instrumental in the early, fierce resistance against the conquistador Alonso Fernández de Lugo and his forces. While direct accounts of Pelicar's specific military actions are scarce, it is highly probable he contributed warriors to the Guanche confederation that inflicted a devastating defeat upon the Castilians in the First Battle of Acentejo in 1494. However, after the subsequent Castilian victories, particularly the decisive Second Battle of Acentejo and the Battle of La Laguna (Aguere) in 1495, which resulted in heavy Guanche losses and the deaths of key leaders, the strategic situation became untenable.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pelicar's role as a Guanche mencey during the Castilian conquest of Tenerife marks him as a key figure in the regional narrative of indigenous resistance against European expansion, contributing to the complete annexation of the Canary Islands into the Spanish Crown. His surrender in 1496 symbolizes the end of Guanche sovereignty and had lasting consequences for the demographic and cultural landscape of the islands.
